lens: AD EFFECTIVENESS (performance-marketing creative lead, Instagram Stories). I judged each spec on: whether the first second stops the thumb, brand by about 2 s, product clarity, offer clarity, CTA legibility and hold, read times per line, safe zones, and fit with a calm, premium, hand-made brand. I weighted the first 3 s most, because Story drop-off is steep, and anything shown after about 8 s reaches only a fraction of viewers.

scores.reasons: STRONGEST HOOK OF THE THREE. On frame 0 the word "S l o w" (Cormorant 400 px, S1/Slow) is already readable and its tracking is collapsing (STACK_SPACING 56 → −8, 0–0.6). Then "down." drops letter by letter in terracotta (S1/Down/d…., 0.6–1.27). The copy is a direct command to the scrolling thumb, so it stops the scroll in exactly one second. PRODUCT AND PRICE ARE THE LARGEST: "Ash Vase" at 230 px (S3/Headline) and "$48" at 220 px (S3/Price, overshoot 4.8–5.43) sit over the native-resolution vase (#2), with the price readable about 1.6 s. BEST OFFER: a full-screen terracotta field with "10%" at 440 px (S5/Ten, 8.4–9.03), a scale punch on beat 9.0, and "off your first order." word by word. The offer arrives earliest of the three (8.4 s) and is repeated on the end card's URL line ("moku.store · 10% off your first order"). CTA: the offer field contracts into the button (S6/CTA field, 11.0–11.4). That is good conversion logic, because the incentive literally becomes the action. The label is readable 12.15–14.4 (2.25 s), with a ×1.08 pulse, a ping ring and two arrow nudges. BRAND: the top-bar "Moku" is legible by about 1.5 s and stays to 11.0, with colour flips that keep it readable on every background. WEAKNESSES: (1) The brand is a 60 px bug in the corner at y 262, 12 px under Instagram's header, the spot where viewers ignore UI chrome, so its brand salience is low until 11.4. The 22 px Inter label "THE KILN · AUTUMN 2026" is about 8 pt on a phone: unreadable. (2) The pace contradicts the message. Under a "Slow down." headline it runs 6 scenes and 5 transitions in 14.4 s: a 585 px/frame whip with 28 px blur (3.8–4.2), 0.6 s stop-motion product cuts (S4, 6.6–8.4) and a 3-panel burst (8.1–8.4). (3) The collection beat flashes the mug, plates and bowl for about 0.5 s each with no prices, so it conveys range but not product. (4) "Thrown by hand." gets only about 0.75–0.85 s complete before the whip launches at 3.8 (0.9 s needed). "Free shipping over $80" gets about 1.1–1.15 s (1.2 s needed). (5) Frame 0 is mostly cream with a 96 px image slit, so the hook is all type and no product.
scores.keep: The "Slow down." hook: a giant per-letter word readable on frame 0, with its tracking collapsing 0–0.6 s and "down." landing by 1.27 s. It is the only opening of the three that is both a scroll-stopping command and on-brand. A close second: the full-frame "10%" offer field that contracts into the CTA button, with the offer restated on the end-card URL line.
scores.fatal: None fatal. Must fix: (a) a pace and message contradiction, so cut one of the whip or the 3-panel burst and give each collection product at least 0.9 s or drop the collection beat; (b) a low-salience corner brand, so make the bug larger, move it to y ≥ 290, or add a centre brand moment by about 2 s; (c) raise the 22 px label to at least 28 px.

scores.reasons: BEST PRODUCT AND COMMERCE CLARITY. The hero Ash Vase gets 2.4–6.0 s. The dot bursts into a full-width band (Band window, 2.4–2.9) with the vase on the left and the information on the right: "Ash"/"Vase" at 168 px (readable 3.15–5.75), three specs (3.85–5.75), and a "$48" price disc that pops 4.2–4.67, the earliest price of the three. Every collection item gets a name and a price for about 1 s each: "Kiln Mug $32" 5.95–7.0, "Serving Bowl $58" 7.25–8.2, "Dinner Plates $110" 8.45–9.35. "The Kiln collection" holds 6.2–9.4. BEST CTA: a 640 × 120 pill with a 40 px label, readable 11.65–14.4 = 2.75 s (the longest), an 8 % punch at 13.2, a 50 px ripple and two arrow nudges. BEST BRAND CONTINUITY: the "● Moku" bug lands 1.5–1.93, stays on every frame, flips colour as the bloom passes (9.433–9.467) and flies and scales into the end-card logo (11.1–11.533). Read times all pass. The "circle of clay" (wheel, then vase, then window, then button) is coherent with the hand-made brand. WEAKNESSES: (1) Frame 0 is an abstract terracotta disc with a ring arc: no word, no product, no brand. Hands on the wheel appear by 0.3 and "Shaped slowly," by 0.5, so the hook still lands by about 1.0 s. But the copy is descriptive, not a scroll stopper, and a disc with a partial ring can read as a loading spinner. (2) The offer is readable only about 1.0–1.2 s ("10% off" 9.75–10.95) and does NOT reappear on the end card. The footer carries only shipping and plastic-free, so the CTA asks for a click with no incentive visible. (3) The brand bug is 60 px at y 264, tight under the IG header. The collection names and prices sit at y 1500–1580, exactly on the bottom safe-zone line with zero margin. The 22–24 px Inter kickers ("NO. 01", "AUTUMN 2026") are too small to read, and "NO. 01" means nothing to a shopper. (4) The products are small: in a 600 × 760 pill window at 0.5–0.75× scale, less thumb-stopping than full-width imagery. (5) Stacked wipes, slamming cut plates and double blooms lean toward an agency-reel feel rather than calm.
scores.keep: The brand bug that arrives by about 1.9 s, stays on screen through every scene (with colour flips for legibility) and flies and scales into the end-card logo at 11.1–11.533. It fixes the old ad's 9.1 s brand reveal more robustly than either alternative. Second keep: the hero-product information stack (name, specs and a price disc all on screen before 4.7 s) and the 2.75 s CTA hold.
scores.fatal: Near-fatal for a discount-driven ad: "10% off your first order" gets only about 1.2 s (9.75–10.95) and is absent from the end card. Fix: add it to the end-card footer or URL line. Also, frame 0 has no message.

scores.reasons: BEST BRAND TIMING AND MOST PREMIUM MOOD. "M o k u" sits at 104 px, centred, on frame 0 (S1 Row Moku), over the most on-brand full-bleed image (#3, hand-built vessels, at native resolution). Its tracking locks at 1.8. "Made slow." at 230 px is readable by about 0.9 (S1 T s…dot by 1.267). The full-bleed photography, rack focus, wheel-to-vase match cut on the same 790 px circle (4.2), and the dark kiln-arch end card (#5) feel the most like a luxury product film. It is also the only spec that places the breath where the bar asks, directly before the end card (10.233–10.8). Its end card consolidates every conversion element: logo, "10% off your first order" at 60 px (11.95–14.4), CTA (12.1–14.4, about 2.1–2.3 s after the label resolves inside the opening pill), "moku.store" and the shipping line. WEAKNESSES: (1) Frame 0 is deliberately soft: the S1 Plate is at blur 12 and pulls focus only by 0.6. A soft first frame reads as loading or low quality, and it breaks the bar's "clean first frame". (2) The offer never gets a hero beat. It first appears at 11.95 s as a 60 px serif line under a 200 px logo, the latest and smallest offer of the three, seen only by viewers who survive 12 s. (3) Product information arrives late. The vase appears at 4.2, but its name only at 5.0–5.6 and "$48" at 6.0–6.4 (readable 6.15–7.33). (4) The collection is a truck with 20 px whip blurs at 9.0 and 9.6. "Plates" is readable 0.35 s (9.2–9.55) while its image is mid-whip, so the product is shown but not seen. No collection prices. (5) After 2.63 s the brand disappears until 11.4. (6) The camera is the most aggressive of the three for a "slow" brand: an 820 px/frame whip-tilt with SCALE_Y smear (2.17–2.63), a 2.6× push-through dive (7.4–7.8) and two truck whips. The OVERLAY grain at 0.5 opacity risks muddying cream and small type. "Made" (y 262) and the S4 title (y 268) sit tight under the IG header.
scores.keep: Brand on frame 0: a centred, crisp "M o k u" (104 px) over full-bleed hand-built vessels, with its tracking locking shut on beat 1.8. It is the most salient brand reveal, in the centre of attention rather than a corner bug. Also keep its end-card logic: offer, CTA, URL and shipping together on screen for at least 2.1 s, after a breath placed directly before the end card.
scores.fatal: Two flaws that sink it as the spine: the offer is buried (first seen at 11.95 s as a 60 px line, with no hero beat), and the first frame is soft (12 px blur until 0.6 s). Both can be fixed, but both work against the hook and the conversion goals.

recommendation:
Build the final ad on the TYPE spec: its hook, its huge price and its offer are the most effective. Then graft on the best of the other two.

1. HOOK (keep from Type): frame 0 = \"S l o w\" readable and collapsing its tracking, with \"down.\" landing by about 1.27 s. Widen the opening image slit faster, or start it at 240 px, so the product registers by 0.6 s.

2. BRAND (from Camera and Graphic): add a centre brand moment by about 1.8 s instead of relying only on the 60 px corner bug at y 262. Either use Camera's tracking-lock on \"Moku\" (its centred 104 px wordmark), or enlarge the bug and move it to y ≥ 290. Then use Graphic's continuity: the bug stays on through every scene and flies and scales into the end-card logo.

3. PRODUCT (merge Type and Graphic): keep the 230 px \"Ash Vase\" and the 220 px \"$48\" landing by 5.4 s. Replace the 0.5 s stop-motion collection flashes with Graphic's name + price per item at ≥ 0.9 s each, or cut to two products. Keep all collection text ≥ 40 px above y 1580.

4. OFFER (Type): keep the full-frame terracotta \"10%\" field that contracts into the CTA button. Restate \"10% off your first order\" on the end card, as Type's URL line or Camera's 60 px row; Graphic's omission of it is the trap to avoid. Consider a small offer tease earlier (for example in the S3 spec stack, by about 6 s), because most Story viewers never reach 8.4 s.

5. CTA (Graphic's numbers): a pill of at least 600 × 116 with a label of at least 40 px. Label readable for at least 2.5 s (Graphic's 2.75 s), one 8 % punch with settle, a ripple and two arrow nudges. Put Camera's breath directly before the end card.

6. PACE AND BRAND FIT: \"Slow down.\" cannot be followed by the busiest edit. Remove one high-energy transition, either the 3-panel burst or the whip (ideally drop the separate \"Thrown by hand.\" scene, or give it ≥ 1.0 s complete). Keep peak blurs at or below 20 px.

7. LEGIBILITY HYGIENE (all three specs): no Inter label below 28 px (the 22–24 px eyebrows and kickers are unreadable on a phone). Keep all text at y ≥ 280 and ≤ 1540 for margin against Instagram's chrome. A clean, sharp frame 0, so no Camera-style rack-focus blur on the opening. Grain optional and subtle, or none.
